raw_response:
I am old now, and with only 5 mu I cannot spread myself too wide. This year I will still keep both cotton and maize, same as I know, but I will not do anything too risky. Cotton brings cash if it does well, but it needs more hand work. Maize is steadier and easier to manage. So I will put a bit more land into cotton because I know that crop well, and keep some maize so I am not depending on one thing only. I do not read fertilizer numbers the way technicians do. I farm by what I have seen: if the crop looks weak, I add a bit more; if money is tight, I hold back. I have a well, so if the sky stays dry, I can save the crop with one or two irrigations, but pumping costs money, so I will not water unless the field really needs it.

For cotton, I will plant after the soil warms in late April. I will buy the same local hybrid seed people nearby use, not the expensive fancy kind. I will put most fertilizer at the start, then add one more time when the plants are growing fast if they look hungry. Cotton needs more weeding, spraying, and picking, and at my age that is hard, so if both of us at home cannot finish, I will hire a little help at picking time. For maize, I will plant in late April to early May. Maize is simpler. I will put fertilizer once at planting and once when it gets knee-high. If there is enough rain, I may only irrigate once, but if early summer is dry, I will use the well. I will spray herbicide once and only use insecticide if I see pests.
